newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt, futures nervous ahead of FOMC meeting.
newsitem.headline: German debt, futures nervous ahead of FOMC meeting.

text.p: German Bunds and futures were slightly higher in late trade but off the session lows, weighed on by a drop in the dollar and narrow losses in U.S. debt markets, traders said.
At 1605 GMT, DTB June Bund futures were up 17 basis points at 99.86 points but well below the session high reached in earlier dealings at 100.25 points.

Traders said they looked for neutral dealings on Monday ahead of the FOMC's policy meeting that starts on Tuesday. The German market generally expects the Federal Reserve to raise short-term interest rates at the meeting.
German data played a minimal role in the market, which showed a negligible reaction to a report showing producer prices were unchanged in February.
"We've had a bit of a shortcovering rally today but the market is generally lacking much interest," one trader said.
"And if U.S. markets show any weakness after the European close, we will likely test some new lows on Monday," he said.
Dealers said the market was driven by technical factors and said June Bunds had fallen to retrace a gap at 99.95 in order for a move toward 100.34.
